references.text: Jesus answers the woman with the same words he used when asking about her accusers: 'Where are they?', and confirms that no one has condemned her, before giving her a new command to sin no more.
In the previous verse, Jesus throws down his stone and challenges anyone without sin to cast the first stone, creating the context for why no accusers remain when he asks, 'Where are they?'
The verse describes Jesus sitting in the temple, the same place where the incident with the woman caught in adultery takes place, and where he later stands up to speak to her.
Shortly after showing mercy and not condemning the woman, Jesus proclaims himself as 'the light of the world', a theme connected to his role as a judge who does not condemn.
Jesus confirms later in the same chapter that he does not seek his own glory or judgment, but that it is the Father who judges, underscoring his attitude of not condemning the woman earlier.
